questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Spot a claim that names no agent
questions.stem: A beekeeper writes 'The hive was treated.' Why is this claim weak?

options.text: It names no one who performed the treatment.
The hive is not a valid subject.

questions.explanation: The claim names no agent, so responsibility and method stay hidden. Active voice fixes it.

provenance.author: bank-team-english-language
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.stem: A beekeeper's paragraph promises 'three causes of swarm loss' but lists only two. What is broken?

answer.exemplar: The opening promise is not fulfilled because the paragraph delivers fewer items than it announced.

questions.explanation: A paragraph must deliver what its opening promises. Listing two causes after promising three breaks that contract.

provenance.author: bank-team-english-language
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE

stimulus.body: The logbook says: 'It is said that queens fail in cold snaps.' No source is given.

questions.stem: What is the main problem with this sentence?

options.text: The reported speech has no named source.

options.misconception: reported speech is allowed with attribution

questions.explanation: 'It is said' hides the source. Naming who says it, or replacing the claim with data, would fix the problem.

provenance.author: bank-team-english-language
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE

stimulus.body: A beekeeper writes 'First, check the entrance. Second, ignore the weather. Finally, harvest.'

questions.stem: Which signpost misleads the reader?

options.text: 'Second, ignore the weather' is not a real step.

questions.explanation: 'Second, ignore the weather' is not a genuine step, so the signpost misleads. Removing or replacing it restores honesty.

provenance.author: bank-team-english-language
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.learningObjective: Keep a claim within a source's scope
questions.stem: A study covers only spring colonies. Which claim respects its scope?

options.text: 'All colonies everywhere lose more in spring.'

questions.explanation: Option A keeps the claim inside the study's spring scope. The others generalise beyond the evidence.

questions.subject: ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
questions.topic: A source narrower than the claim
questions.learningObjective: Spot a claim wider than its source

questions.explanation: A single hive is narrower than a regional claim. The conclusion overreaches the evidence.
